page.text:
The *center* $Z(G)$ of a group comprises all elements that commute with
every element of the group:
$Z(G) = \{z \in G : z * g = g * z \text{ for all } g \in G\}$. The center
measures the degree of commutativity of $G$: $Z(G) = G$ if and only if
$G$ is abelian, while for non-abelian simple groups $Z(G)$ is trivial.
